name: Gargamelle
summary: Gargamelle discovered weak neutral currents in neutrino interactions at CERN, providing decisive experimental support for electroweak unification.
detection_principle: Charged secondaries formed bubble tracks in dense liquid freon. Neutral-current candidates contained an interaction vertex and hadrons or an electron, without the outgoing charged muon expected from a muon-neutrino charged-current interaction.

status.label: Completed / historical

key_parameters.name: Chamber dimensions
key_parameters.value: About 4.8 m long and 2 m diameter

key_parameters.name: Active liquid
key_parameters.value: Nearly 12 cubic metres of heavy freon, CF3Br

key_parameters.name: Beam sites
key_parameters.value: CERN Proton Synchrotron, then Super Proton Synchrotron

results.summary: Established both hadronic and leptonic neutral-current evidence, an essential test of the electroweak theory.

science_scope: The record describes the named experiment as one programme; detector subsystems and repeated analyses are not counted as independent experiments.
